questions.question: The Harappan brought Gold from present-day _______ in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Karnataka__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bronze Age civilization included the Harappan culture.**
 
• Objects connected to **copper, bronze, gold, silver, and lead** are visible.
 
• With the exception of iron, practically **all metals were known to the Harappans.**
 
• They **produced items made of gold and silver.**
 
 
• It's possible that **South India's riverbeds (Karnataka) and the Himalayas provided gold,** while Mesopotamia provided silver.
 
• **Beads, armlets, needles, and other accessories are among the gold items.**
 
• Silver, however, was used more frequently than gold.
 
• There have been many silver plates, decorations, and other items found.
 
 
 
• Moreover, a variety of copper tools and weapons have been found.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka**

 
 
• Current Chief Minister is** **Siddaramaiah. (June 2023)
 
• Current Governor is **Thawar Chand Gehlot**. (April 2023)
 
• The state of Karnataka was formed in** 1956** and renamed as Karnataka in **1973**.
 
• The capital of Karnataka is **Bengaluru**.
 
• The official language of Karnataka is** Kannada**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the component of the capital expenditure of the Government?

options.text: Expenditure on the acquisition of machinery
Expenditure on the acquisition of land
Expenditure on the acquisition of building

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Interest payments__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Capital expenditure**

 
 
• The **money that the government spends on developing buildings, machinery, equipment, schools and other infrastructure is known as capital expenditure.**
 
• Additionally, it **covers the costs made by the government for investments that will generate profits or dividends in the future,** such as land acquisition costs.
 
• According to the budget, the **government would spend $1,084,748 on capital projects in 2020–21.**
 
• The **2019-20 Budget's revised capital expenditure estimates came in at Rs. 1,059,472 crores,** while the 2018-19 Budget's actual capital expenditures came in at Rs. 915,670 crores.
 
• **Spending on investments or development is referred to as capital spending, **and these types of expenditures have long-term advantages.
 
• The following **expenses are included in capital expenditures:**
 
 
• Purchasing fixed and immovable assets
 
• Enhancing a current asset
 
• Restoring a current asset
 
• Repayment of a loan

questions.question: Which of the following has become the first state in the country to get the L-root server?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan.**__

__
 
• **Rajasthan** has been the first State in the nation to **receive the L-root server, **allowing the **State government to enforce e-governance and offer its signature digital services** with seamless** internet connectivity**.
 
• The new facility will **help increase the security and resilience** of internet-based businesses while strengthening internet infrastructure.
 
• In collaboration with the **Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers,** the new server has been set up in the Bhamashah State Data Centre here (ICANN).

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which minorities are mentioned in article 30 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Linguistic and religious__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Minorities are granted the freedom to create and run their educational institutions. **Also known as the "Charter of Education Rights," Article 30.
 
• **Article 30(1)**
 
 
• All minorities must have the freedom to create and run the educational institutions of their choice, regardless of whether they are classified as religious or linguistic minorities.
 
• 1 (A):
 
 
• The State shall ensure that the **amount fixed by or determined under such law for the acquisition of any property** of an educational institution established and administered by a minority, as referenced in clause (1), is such as would not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed under that clause.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Article 30(2)**
 
 
• The **state is prohibited from discriminating against any educational institution** on the grounds that it is run by a minority, regardless of their religion or language, while providing financial support to educational institutions.​​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution went into effect on **January 26, 1950.** The Constitution was the longest national constitution ever approved at the time of its ratification.
 
• It had **395 Articles, 8 Schedules, and was about 145,000 words long.**
 
• During the course of 11 sessions and 167 days, spanning two years and eleven months, the members of the Constituent Assembly deliberated on every article of the Constitution.
 
• The **Articles are divided into 22 different portions**, which corresponds to how the **Constitution of India, 1950's** text has them arranged.
 
• The** Schedules to the Constitution, **which now** number 12,** give into more detail about government policy or regulations in respect to particular Constitutional Articles.

questions.question: Which of the following climate type is found under the cold climates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Tundra__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Among all the **biomes,** the **tundra is the coldest.**
 
• In addition, the **tundra experiences little precipitation,** which resembles a desert.
 
• **Arctic tundra can be found **in the areas immediately **below the ice caps**, and it can be found **in Siberia in Asia, North America, and Europe.**
 
• The tundra biome **encompasses most of Alaska and roughly half of Canada.**
 
• Several places throughout the world also have **tundra on the summits of very tall mountains.**
 
• With mean **annual temperatures below 0°C during six to ten months of the year,** tundra winters are protracted, dark, and cold.
 
• Permafrost, or permanently frozen ground, results from the area's extremely low temperatures.
 
• The tundra biome is distinguished by this permafrost.
 
• Only a few inches of the top layer of soil thaws during the tundra summers, giving vegetation roots a growth surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Humid subtropical:**

 
 
• **​**A climate zone characterised mid summers and cold to mild winters is known as a humid subtropical climate.
 
 
 
• **Highland:**
 
 
• Highland climate features include high insolation, low temperatures, low air pressure, wide diurnal temperature fluctuations, and relatively heavy precipitation at higher altitudes.
 
 
 
• **Humid continental:**
 
 
• It is characterized by four distinct seasons, significant seasonal temperature changes, and frigid (often extremely cold) winters.

questions.question: The mass number of potassium is ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**39.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We know that** mass no. is given as**,

 
 
• Mass no.= No. of protons + No. of neutrons.
 
 
 
• **Potassium has an atomic number of 19**, and an element's atomic number is determined by how many protons it contains.
 
• Hence, **potassium contains 19 protons.**
 
• **Twenty neutrons** make up potassium.
 
• The **mass number of potassium is calculated **using the formula above as,
 
 
• Mass no. = 20+19=39. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Potassium is a member of the alkali group of the periodic table.
 
 
• Symbol: K.
 
• Atomic number: 19.
 
• Belongs to group 1 in the periodic table.
 
• First isolated in 1807 by Humphry Davy.
 
• Sodium and Potassium are the elements known as soft metals(can cut with a knife with little force).
 
• Potassium metal is kept in kerosene due to its high reactivity with water.
 
• Potassium bicarbonate is the chemical used in fire extinguishers.
 
• Potassium is the most common radioisotope in the human body.
 
• Potassium is the second least dense metal after lithium.

questions.question: What do you call the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary productivity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary productivity **is the pace at which producers - plants and other photosynthetic organisms - create new organic matter.
 
• The **rate at which consumers are creating new organic matter** is known as **secondary productivity. **Protists, fungi, bacteria, Deer, cows, goats, horses, etc. are a few examples.
 
• The entire **dry biomass of all living things at a certain trophic level** is referred to as a **standing crop.**
 
• It stands for biomass that is above ground. It could vary during the course of the year.
 
• There are** two forms of primary productivity:**
 
 
• Gross primary productivity, which measures the total rate of photosynthesis and the amount of organic matter consumed during respiration and is influenced by chlorophyll content.
 
• The difference between gross primary production and ecosystem organisms' respiration is known as net primary production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tertiary productivity:****​**

 
 
• **​**The quantity of fresh biomass (weight) that carnivores (animals that eat meat) create over a certain amount of time.
 
 
 
• **Primary Productivity:**
 
 
• **​**The process by which organisms produce their own sustenance from inorganic sources is known as primary productivity. Terrestrial plants and microbiological life, such as algae, make up the majority of primary producers.
 
 
 
• **Net Productivity:**
 
 
• **​**The total amount of food or biomass produced by primary producers minus energy losses, which is also the total amount of food stored by producers, is referred to as net primary productivity.

questions.question: What is the structure of the Indian judiciary?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Three-tier**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Indian judiciary is organized into a three-tier system:
 
• **Supreme Court: **
 
 
• At the top is the Supreme Court of India, which is the highest judicial authority in the country.
 
• It has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power to hear appeals from lower courts, issue writs, and interpret the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **High Courts: **
 
 
• Each state in India has a High Court.
 
• High Courts are the second-highest courts in the country and have jurisdiction over their respective states or union territories.
 
• They have the power of superintendence over the subordinate courts within their jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Subordinate Courts:**
 
 
• The third tier consists of the subordinate courts, which include District Courts, Sessions Courts, and other lower courts.
 
• These courts are established by the state governments and are responsible for hearing civil and criminal cases within their territorial jurisdiction.
 
• District Courts are at the lowest level and are presided over by District Judges.

questions.question: Which enzyme in the pancreatic juice helps in breaking down fats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lipase.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lipase,** 

 
 
• **Triglycerides are broken down by a class of enzymes called lipases into free fatty acids and glycerol.**
 
• They are present and functional in a variety of tissues; for instance, hepatic lipases are found in the liver, hormone-sensitive lipases in adipocytes, lipoprotein lipase is found on the surface of vascular endothelial cells, and pancreatic lipase is found in the small intestine.
 
• This enzyme functions in conjunction with the bile your liver produces.
 
• Your body will have problems absorbing fat and the crucial fat-soluble vitamins if you don't have enough lipase (A, D, E, K).
 
• Poor fat absorption is characterized by diarrhea and greasdiarrheay bowel motions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protease,**

 
 
• Proteases have more specialised uses in the extraction of mucopolysaccharides and carbohydrate gums, which are nonprotein compounds made from animal or plant extracts.
 
• Proteases can be employed to dissolve keratin-containing materials, such as feather debris, to provide protein concentrates for animal diets. Streptomyces species' alkaline proteases have potent keratinolytic activity as well.
 
• Your diet's protein is broken down by this enzyme.
 
• Also, it aids in defending you against microorganisms like certain bacteria and yeast that could reside in your intestines.
 
 
 
• **Amylase,**
 
 
• Any member of the class of enzymes known as amylases is responsible for catalysing the breakdown of starch into smaller carbohydrate molecules like maltose (a molecule composed of two glucose molecules). 
 
• Alpha-amylase is present in many biological things.
 
• Ptyalin, an alpha-amylase produced by salivary glands in the digestive tracts of humans and many other mammals, is secreted into the small intestine by pancreatic amylase.
 
• The undigested carbs may cause diarrhea if you don't have enough amylase.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin,**
 
 
• Pepsin, a potent digestive enzyme found in gastric juice, breaks down proteins found in foods including meat, eggs, seeds, and dairy products.
 
• The mature active version of the inactive protein pepsinogen is called pepsin.
 
• Pepsinogen is produced and stored by glands in the mucous membrane lining of the stomach. Pepsinogen is released into the stomach under the influence of vagus nerve impulses and the hormonal secretions gastrin and secretin, where it is combined with hydrochloric acid and quickly transformed into the active enzyme pepsin.

questions.question: Name the two states in which land reform were successful?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__West Bengal and Kerala__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of independence, the land tenure system was under the control of zamindars who were only responsible for the collection of revenue and they did not contribute to renovating or modernizing farmlands.
 
• Land reforms were fruitful in Kerala and West Bengal because these states had governments who were committed to the policy of land to the tiller and they brought necessary legislations for the same.
 
• Bhoodan and Gramodan movements led by Vinoba Bhave played role in land reforms in Zamindari areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In West Bengal due to “Operation Barga” maximum sharecroppers were given ownership of land.
 
• Cooperative farming is advocated to solve the problem of sub-divisions of landholdings.
 
• Main objectives of Land Reforms-
 
 
• To legitimize tenancy with the ceiling limit.
 
• To register all the tenancy with the village Panchayats.
 
• To establish a relation between tenancy and ceiling.
 
• To remove rural poverty.
 
• Proliferating socialist development to lessen social inequality
 
• Empowerment of women in the traditionally male-driven society.

questions.question: In which game/sport is the area of bout called a ring?

questions.question: Ekaharya is the solo artist in which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatnatyam** (Tamil Nadu)

 
 
• **One of the primary texts used to study the technique and grammar of body movement in Bharatnatyam dance** is the Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikesvara.
 
• In **Bharatnatyam dance, one dancer plays various characters in a single performance, a technique known as ekaharya.**
 
• **Leg, hip, and arm transitional movements are used in the dance.**
 
• The dance has **seven primary sections **that are typically split down into Alarippu, Jatiswaran, Shabda, Varna, Pada, Thillana, and Sloka.
 
• The **Chidambaram temple's gopurams **feature Bharatnatyam positions (Tamil Nadu).
 
• **E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale were instrumental in restoring the dance's standing and popularity.**
 
• **​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak**

 
 
• **​**The idea of storytelling is central to Kathak, one of India's most exquisite dance styles. Kathak, the sole dance from northern India among the eight Indian classical dance styles, is an art form with an enigmatic beauty, captivating footwork, and beautiful motions.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• **​**Kuchipudi is renowned for its dynamic storytelling, dramatic characterization, outstanding, rapid dancing, and expressive eye movements. Tandava (the regal, masculine) and Lasya are combined in this dance (lyrical graceful and feminine energy).
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**
 
 
• **​**The traditional solo dancing style of Kerala is called Mohiniyattam, which is simply translated as "the dance of Mohini," the celestial enchantress from Hindu mythology.

• The FATF stated that the new president would** prioritize increasing asset recovery**, as well as the efficiency of international **anti-money laundering** and counter-terrorism funding measures.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated on the last day of the holy month of Ramadan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Eid-ul-Fitr__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eid ul-Fitr** is a significant Islamic holiday that starts the minute the new moon is sighted,** marks the conclusion **of the month-long fasting of Ramadan.
 
• The only day in the month of Shawwal when Muslims are **not allowed to fast **is this religious Eid.
 
• Fasting during the month of** Ramadan** is one of the most significant Islamic practices, and it is one of the most important festivals observed by Muslims worldwide.
 
• One of the** five pillars of Islam** is the Ramadan fast.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milad-un-Nabi:**

 
 
• ​The yearly festival of Eid Milad-un-Nabi **honours the birthday of Prophet Muhammad**, takes place in Rabi-ul-Awwal, the third month of the Islamic lunar calendar, which begins with the sighting of the moon.
 
• The date **also commemorates the Prophet's passing anniversary.**
 
 
 
• **Shab-e-Barat:** **​**
 
 
• **​**The Muslim festival of Shab-e-Barat commemorates the **halfway point of the month before Ramadan**, has arrived.
 
 
 
• **Eid-ul-zuha:**
 
 
• ​​**The Feast of Sacrifice**, also known as Eid al-Zuha, is one of the most important Islamic holidays.
 
• The enthralling chants of** 'Allah hu Akbar'** are spread throughout the world during the exuberant Eid ul-zuha celebrations.
 
• While it is known as **Bakr-id in India**, it is also known as Eid al-Adha, Id-ul-zuha, Id-ul-Azha, and Hari Raya Haji in other nations.
 
• On the** tenth day** of the **lunar-based** Islamic calendar's **12th month**, this auspicious day is observed.
